arguments.decision: How should the Anastrophe BLE "Tap" flow scan for readers so that the R1 app meets its latency target while keeping strongest-reader selection?
arguments.evidence: SDD §6.3 Tap flow (LAContext auth; 5 s scan filtered by service UUID; strongest reader above per-reader threshold e.g. -55 dBm per FR-83; connect/MTU/ANP/1/RESULT/disconnect; max 1 txn per 3 s per reader). NFR-P04: intent to reader decision <= 1.5 s p95. FR-80, FR-83, O-B04, O-B01. Current LiveBLECentral.scan always sleeps the full 5 s; an independent code reviewer flagged that NFR-P04 / TC-PRSB-01 then fail deterministically (plan/SDD contradiction). Reader advertising intervals typically 100-250 ms; Face ID precedes scanning and takes several hundred ms.
arguments.priorities: Meet NFR-P04 (<= 1.5 s p95 intent-to-decision) in the R1 pilots; keep FR-83; stay foreground-only (ADR-0012); keep the implementation simple and testable without hardware.
requirements: Can achieve intent-to-decision <= 1.5 s at p95 when a reader is within ~30 cm (NFR-P04).
Processes only the strongest reader at or above the RSSI threshold (FR-83).
Performs no Bluetooth scanning while the app is in the background (ADR-0012).
